newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian, Israeli talks on boosting economic ties.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian, Israeli talks on boosting economic ties.

text.p: Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan discussed on Tuesday with an Israeli team headed by Finance Minister Dan Meridor joint industrial projects in the Jordan Valley border region, officials said.
They said the focus of the one-day talks with the Israeli delegation, which includes senior businessmen, was on major projects to develop the valley.

"Mr Meridor reaffirmed Israel's commitment to the concept of Jordan Rift Valley development and agreed with Crown Prince Hassan that practical steps ought to be implemented with urgency," said a palace spokesman.

The talks began on the Jordanian side of the Dead Sea, with discussion of projects along the valley such as establishment of a park at the lowest point on earth, industrial zones, a fibre optic communications network and agricultural cooperation.
Israeli embassy spokesman Shalom Tourgeman said the two sides emphasised the importance of promoting the Middle East peace process by expanding joint ventures.

The Israeli embassy says so far around 15 projects in Jordan have been set up or are in the pipeline with Israeli capital since the two countries signed a peace treaty in 1994, ending a 46-year state of war.
But many Jordanians are cool to forging close ties with Israel and its first trade fair in Amman last week touched off protests by anti-Israeli demonstrators.
